headline: IPO ambitions. Ground stations. Satellite constellations.
deck: This week, we see a mix of IPO aspirations and strategic acquisitions in the space sector.

stories.head: MinoSpace eyes $736 million IPO for expansion
stories.body: Chinese satellite maker MinoSpace is seeking $736 million in its upcoming IPO to expand its satellite constellation. This move reflects the ongoing appetite for satellite services, particularly in the commercial sector. If successful, MinoSpace could join the ranks of other notable Chinese space firms looking to capitalize on the growing demand for data services.
stories.soWhat: MinoSpace's IPO could signal a shift in investor sentiment towards Chinese tech, but it remains to be seen if they can deliver on their growth promises.

stories.head: Intuitive Machines buys ground station firm
stories.body: Intuitive Machines has announced its acquisition of a ground station company to enhance its lunar communications capabilities. The financial details were not disclosed, but this move is part of Intuitive's broader strategy to ensure reliable communication for its lunar missions. Given the challenges of lunar operations, a robust ground station network is crucial.
stories.soWhat: This acquisition underscores the increasing importance of ground infrastructure in supporting lunar ambitions, a lesson that many companies still overlook.

stories.head: Cowboy Space files for 20,000 satellites
stories.body: Cowboy Space has filed plans for a constellation of up to 20,000 satellites, aiming to create a massive orbital data center network. This ambitious proposal highlights the trend of scaling satellite constellations to meet burgeoning data demands. While the feasibility remains in question, the sheer number indicates a belief that more satellites can solve more problems.
stories.soWhat: In a world where bandwidth is king, Cowboy's plans could either be visionary or a classic case of overreach—time will tell.

watchlist.title: Virgin Galactic's commercial service timeline
watchlist.body: Virgin Galactic insists on launching commercial flights by year-end; skepticism remains about their ability to meet this deadline.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle test delays
watchlist.body: With the hypersonic glide-vehicle test slipping again, the defense sector may need to rethink its timelines and expectations.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program could indicate a shift in defense procurement strategies focusing on software solutions.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's growth trajectory
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C could position it as a key player in co-orbital security, especially with DoD backing.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
